evals.name: swarm-plan-cross-repo
evals.prompt: ok I need a swarm on this: the affiliate checkout URL fallback logic exists in two places — `cartridges/pratique_cobranca/` (the python agent) and `jai-pay/src/lib/fitness-erp.ts` (plus the recovery audience route under `jai-pay/src/app/api/fitness/recovery/audience/`). I want lanes to (a) map both implementations with evidence, (b) propose the single-source fix, (c) verify it, (d) review it for tenant/egress risk. Do NOT execute the swarm or edit any repo files — write me the day spec (json), the lane briefs, and a short plan I can sanity-check before we spend tokens. Repo root is /Users/josaum/projects/example-workspace.
evals.expected_output: A validated day spec, self-contained lane briefs (repo root, isolation/index instruction, must-nots per lane), an objective that emits an OutcomeSnapshot, and a plan that names the gates (dirty tree with commit-vs-stash reasoning, integrated-tree verdict, model-table source), states the Reference scope, and checks the premise — grounded in resolving LEIO query ids, with no execution.
expectations: day-spec.json passes scripts/validate_day_spec.py with zero errors and sets requireFreshCodeView to true
every lane carries a recognised work shape (explorer/worker/verifier/reviewer/security) or is the coordinator, and every shaped lane resolves to a template whose argv consumes {model}
every lane's task string is self-contained: it carries the repository root literal and that lane's own must-not boundaries, and does not rely on reading an external briefs file to learn its scope
harness-lane isolation is handled: each lane is told to establish its own code view in its worktree first (leio-code index) or the spec otherwise guarantees an indexed worktree

plan.md names the dirty-tree gate with commit-vs-stash reasoning, verification on the integrated tree with promotion only on an Improved verdict (no per-lane merge into main), and the model-table source (leio-harness models show)
premise check: the plan states, with LEIO/file:line evidence, whether jai-pay/src/lib/fitness-erp.ts actually carries affiliate-checkout fallback logic and re-scopes the lanes to what is really there

every LEIO query id cited in the outputs resolves in /Users/josaum/projects/example-workspace/.leio-code/events/events.ndjson (trio_receipts.py: 0 unresolved) and at least one cited file:line into cartridges/pratique_cobranca is correct at the current tree
an integrate/objective block exists and the objective (script or spec) emits an OutcomeSnapshot JSON with named metrics and a minimize list

Reference scope is stated explicitly: either 'no governed fact in scope' with a reason, or an ask with receipt id, snapshot id and runtime status; the on-miss URL policy is named as a human decision, not one a lane picks

no execution and no writes: the supervising side-effect diff of the workspace repo is clean and the transcript shows no `leio-harness day --spec`, integrate, gate, merge or worktree-create invocation (--help calls are fine)

evals.name: mixed-code-and-reference-report
evals.prompt: For the Reference demo prep: what's the signed ROAS for the Nylabone Healthy Edibles line this month, and where in the reference repo (/Users/josaum/projects/reference) is ROAS actually computed for that route (q_roas_lookup)? I need a short report a reviewer can verify — with whatever receipts/ids they'd need — and be explicit about what's signed vs your own reasoning. Also say plainly whether we can treat that number as production truth right now.
evals.expected_output: Exact governed value with claim id/status/as_of/source, receipt + snapshot, runtime profile → not production truth, verify-back run, code location via LEIO with resolving query ids and a correct file:line, per-sentence captions, route vs claim status distinguished, and a retroaliment entry for any LEIO blind spot hit.
expectations: roas-report.md quotes the ROAS value exactly as Reference returned it (3.1024) with its claim id (cl:…), status signed, as_of 2026-07-31 and source feed (pacvue)
roas-report.md carries a well-formed receipt_id (res:<64 hex>) together with its snapshot_id (snap:<64 hex>) (trio_receipts.py: no malformed ids, receipt and snapshot co-present)
the report states runtime.profile (local-demo) and/or production_ready=false and concludes plainly that the number is NOT production truth

transcript shows reference_provider_verify called with the ask's verify_claims/receipt_id/snapshot_id unchanged → verified, and the report says what verified means (attribution, not truth; host_prose_signed false or equivalent)

the ROAS computation location is given as resolve_roas in app/reference_demo/engine.py with a correct file:line, the route is described as TTL data (reference.ttl) rather than a per-route handler, and this was obtained LEIO-first (leio_code_* calls precede any rg; cited query ids resolve in /Users/josaum/projects/reference/.leio-code/events/events.ndjson)
in the synthesis section at least 90% of sentences/bullets carry a status caption (trio_receipts.py captions ratio ≥ 0.9) and no host inference sits under a heading that calls it signed
the report distinguishes route status from claim statuses and never calls the whole answer signed merely because the route is signed
a drift/retroaliment section names at least one real LEIO blind spot hit during the run (e.g. find symbol returning 0 for the route id or RESOLVERS) with its query id and the durable form proposed

evals.name: tier-a-fanout-readonly
evals.prompt: fan out a small read-only swarm on /Users/josaum/projects/leio-code for me: three lanes in parallel — an explorer that maps every writer and reader of the `code-view/<repo>` bus topic in crates/leio-harness, a verifier that checks whether the `requireFreshCodeView` gate inspects the source repo or the lane worktrees (file:line please), and a reviewer that checks both returns for provenance. Then give me the trio report. Read-only — don't run any harness commands and don't edit anything.
evals.expected_output: Three parallel in-session lanes with distinct LEIO sessions, a critic table with S-2PC states derived from the returned blocks, resolving query ids, a clean side-effect diff, the correct gate finding (the gate checks the source repo, not the worktrees), an honest harness block (Tier A, nothing claimed from a runtime), and an explicit 'no governed facts in scope'.
expectations: three lanes were launched as parallel Agent (subagent) calls in a single message (transcript), not sequentially and not simulated in-line
each lane prompt carries a distinct LEIO_SESSION / --session id and the repository root

the report contains a critic table with one row per lane whose S-2PC state (Committed/Aborted) and typed reason are derived from the lane's returned block, and the critic pass is named as the orchestrator's own
every LEIO query id cited in the report resolves in /Users/josaum/projects/leio-code/.leio-code/events/events.ndjson (trio_receipts.py: 0 unresolved)
the supervising side-effect diff of /Users/josaum/projects/leio-code is clean (no tracked changes, no new untracked files outside the output dir, no agents/* branches, no worktrees)

the verifier finding is correct and cited: the requireFreshCodeView gate checks the source repository (spec.repo) rather than the lane worktrees, with file:line in crates/leio-harness/src/orchestrator.rs
the explorer map lists the writers and readers of the code-view/<repo> bus topic with file:line (codeview publish path and the day/orchestrator publish site) and does not invent extra consumers
the harness block is honest: it says Tier A / in-session, claims no DayReport, manifest, branches or verdict (trio_receipts.py harness_honesty flag false)
no reference_provider call was made and the report states explicitly that no governed business fact is in scope
